features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience shipping AI or LLM systems in production, especially with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure modes.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Academic preparation
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education or degree attainment the applicant cites as preparation for the role.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree or equivalent preparation is mentioned.
Mentions a bachelor's degree or equivalent.
Mentions a master's degree.
Mentions a doctoral degree.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct experience designing or owning agent-based systems, especially their autonomy boundaries, supervision, control planes, and auditability.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures whether the letter provides concrete evidence of practical command of data structures and algorithms applied to real engineering problems.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Algorithmic fluency is claimed, but without a concrete example.
At least one specific redesign or optimization shows applied algorithmic thinking.
Multiple or especially vivid examples show data structures and algorithms materially shaping system design.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security tooling as helping developers through better defaults, lower friction, and attention to internal users' needs.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates its claims with named examples, mechanisms, measurements, outcomes, or other believable detail rather than generic assertions.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on generic claims, values, or adjectives.
Includes some examples, but the work or outcome remains vague.
Gives concrete examples of what was built, changed, or owned.
Gives concrete examples plus clear mechanisms, outcomes, or measurement that make the impact easy to trust.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a central, meaningful production language for the applicant.

levels.descriptor: Go is missing, unclear, or only incidental.
Go is mentioned as a language used, but not as a main vehicle for work.
Go is clearly presented as the primary or day-to-day language.
Go is central to multiple production systems or explicitly tied to backend or security-infrastructure ownership.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes durability, reliability, failure-awareness, operational care, and disciplined long-term ownership rather than only feature delivery.

levels.descriptor: No maintainer or operational mindset is visible.
Mentions maintenance or testing as duties but does not turn that into a design perspective.
Explicitly frames the applicant as a maintainer who values durability, inheritance, or real-world failure modes.
Uses maintenance or failure experience to explain a clear philosophy for how secure systems should be designed and operated.

features.name: Narrative distinctiveness
features.description: Captures whether the letter has a memorable, non-templated voice or framing that makes the applicant's story stand out.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing attacker-minded practice outside routine job duties, especially through CTFs or similar adversarial exercises.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public or upstream codebases, from fixing dependencies at the source to contributing patches or maintaining projects used by others.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, depth, and seriousness of self-directed projects used to demonstrate curiosity and engineering range outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned.
Mentions a small or utilitarian personal app or tool with limited technical challenge.
Shows a sustained side project with nontrivial systems, infrastructure, or engineering discipline.
Shows an ambitious distributed, reliability-heavy, or failure-oriented project chosen specifically to tackle hard edge cases.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation for foundational or central infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams, products, or users.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the amount, breadth, and maturity of real production software-engineering experience the letter conveys through tenure, shipped systems, and operational ownership.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and credibly the letter shows Python as a serious production language for services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or Python is only named without context.
Python is mentioned for basic scripting or generic use.
Shows substantial production Python use in services, automation, or internal tooling.
Shows deep production Python use with quality signals such as typed, tested, extensible, or central security tooling.

features.name: Role-fit narrative
features.description: Captures how coherently and specifically the letter makes this exact role feel like a logical fit by connecting background, motivation, and posting requirements.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads as a disconnected list of matches to the posting.
The letter is mostly list-like, with only light linking between examples and motivation.
The letter forms a coherent story that joins background, examples, and role fit.
The letter has a strong central thesis or arc that meaningfully organizes the evidence throughout.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience performing security reviews or assessments such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, and remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter understands this role as scaling security work through automation, workflow systems, and high-leverage security tooling rather than generic software engineering.

levels.descriptor: Frames the role generically as software or security work, with little sign of understanding the specific problem the team solves.
Mentions automation or security scale in broad terms, but without a crisp diagnosis of the underlying bottleneck.
Frames the work as reducing manual security workload or improving vulnerability handling at scale.
Articulates a precise thesis about the domain, such as scaling scarce expert judgment, treating vulnerability response as a systems problem, or multiplying one finding into fleet-wide protection.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal external security certifications or other third-party validation of security knowledge and skill.

levels.descriptor: No security credential is mentioned.
Mentions a baseline credential such as Security+ or equivalent fundamentals.
Mentions a demanding practical credential such as OSCP or equivalent.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful, role-relevant view of what security engineering is for and presents the applicant as operating with a genuine security mindset.

levels.descriptor: Little sign of a security-specific philosophy or perspective.
Expresses seriousness about security, but only in generic terms.
Shows a clear personal lens such as attacker thinking, builder's-eye reviewing, or preference for quiet resilience.
Presents a memorable, role-relevant philosophy that convincingly shapes how the applicant builds and evaluates systems.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct ownership of tooling that automates vulnerability-report intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related handling workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface correctness and proofreading quality of the letter, including spelling, grammar, and copy-editing accuracy.

levels.descriptor: Frequent noticeable errors that distract and materially reduce polish.
Several spelling or typographical errors, though the message remains understandable.
Only occasional minor errors; generally polished.
Clean or nearly clean prose with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not cleanly belong to the recurring shared constructs above.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear collaboration or internal-customer orientation.
Uses generic team language, but without a concrete sense of collaborators or users.
Explicitly mentions partnering with security engineers or serving developer teams.
Clearly frames success as collaborative enablement, including learning from specialists and building thoughtfully for other engineers.
